rulings.challenge_claim: The front-seam argument is contradicted by the bytes the unit itself quotes, and the one disclosed cross-seam cohesion device misdescribes the verse it appeals to: the verse named as the source of the recurrence carries a three-item list, not the two-item pairing claimed, and the shared words are not byte-identical.
rulings.grounds: The recurrence half is upheld on the bytes; the front-seam half is narrowed. The unit's closing verse carries the two-item יַ֥יִן וָקַ֖יִץ (oshb:Jer.40.12, byte tier), while the verse named as the source of the recurrence carries a three-item list, יַ֨יִן וְקַ֜יִץ וְשֶׁ֗מֶן (oshb:Jer.40.10, byte tier), matching “gather wine and summer fruits and oil” (web:Jer.40.10). Neither shared word is byte-identical across the two verses: the produce noun agrees only once accents are stripped, and the conjoined word differs in its own vowel, sheva at oshb:Jer.40.10 against qamats at oshb:Jer.40.12, so it agrees only at skeleton tier. The oshb:Jer.40.10 form is spliced in no field of the unit and the recurrence carries no tier label, so a sameness claim stands with no quoted form behind it and on the wrong count object, a pairing named for a three-item list. The front-seam half is narrowed rather than upheld as framed: calling the incoming population unconnected to the captains is byte-true about who the group is, since the Jews in Moab, Ammon and Edom are not the field captains, so the bytes do not contradict it. What is defective there is a disclosure gap of the same class the unit elsewhere honours: its own onset verse opens on the additive particle וְגַ֣ם (oshb:Jer.40.11, byte tier), rendered “Likewise” (web:Jer.40.11), a byte-true continuity signal standing directly across the unit's own front seam and left undisclosed while a different cross-seam device is disclosed.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: replace the phrase making oshb:Jer.40.10 the source of the same pairing with a form-named, tier-labelled statement that splices the oshb:Jer.40.10 list beside the oshb:Jer.40.12 pair, names both count objects (three-item list against two-item pairing), and gives the tier at which each shared word actually agrees; device_notes: re-cut the catchword sentence to that corrected extent. boundary_rationale or device_notes: disclose the verse-initial additive at oshb:Jer.40.11 as cross-seam cohesion, or restate the word 'unconnected' so it does not read against it. Tests the cure must pass: each quoted form re-collates at the tier claimed against its own cited ref, and the recurrence sentence survives the check that killed the original, namely that oshb:Jer.40.10 carries three items and that neither shared word is byte-identical across the two verses.

rulings.challenge_claim: Two challenges: the curly-quoted rendering paired with the byte splice at web:Jer.40.14 is truncated against the staged folded text and drops the disbelief clause; and the ketiv/qere disclosure at oshb:Jer.40.16 names a qere letter that no codepoint in the verse supports.
rulings.grounds: Distinct defects, both byte-confirmed, both upheld. First, the splice for oshb:Jer.40.14 is the entire verse and runs through וְלֹא הֶאֱמִ֣ין לָהֶ֔ם גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן אֲחִיקָֽם (byte tier), but the rendering paired with it stops at the warning question: the staged folded text carries “But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam didn’t believe them.” (web:Jer.40.14) after it and the frame “and said to him,” (web:Jer.40.14) before it. Gloss extent no longer equals splice extent, and the clause that falls out is the refusal to believe on which the unit's own characterisation of the scene turns. The verse is one of the staged continuation-paragraph fold sites, where fidelity is judged against the folded text rather than a re-derived layout. Second, the bytes at oshb:Jer.40.16 read תעש תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה (byte tier): the ketiv תעש is three letters, tav-ayin-shin, and the qere תַּעֲשֵׂ֖ה is four, tav-ayin-sin-he. The disclosure names a five-letter qere closing he-yod; no codepoint in the verse carries a yod. The rationale's own spliced pair is correct, so the error is confined to the letter-naming prose, but it lands on a disclosure offered together with the closing segment mark at the unit's end verse, inside the book's largest such note inventory. Everything else on this unit verifies: four full-verse splices at byte tier, the closing mark correctly typed as setumah and disclosed single-witness, the paseq at oshb:Jer.40.14 cited count-only, and the exclusivity claim for the Ammonite king carrying its own in-sentence digit and byte-true (sweep: 1 verse). The declared heuristic false positives on this unit are confirmed.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: extend the rendering paired with the oshb:Jer.40.14 splice to the whole staged folded verse, opening frame and disbelief clause included. device_notes: correct the qere to its four letters, tav-ayin-sin-he, and delete the yod. Tests the cure must pass: the paired rendering covers the same verse extent as the Hebrew splice at that ref, the check that killed the original being a splice running to the disbelief clause against a rendering stopping at the question; and every letter named in the ketiv/qere sentence is supported by a codepoint in the cited verse.

rulings.challenge_claim: Renderings paired with full-verse splices are truncated at web:Jer.41.8 and web:Jer.41.6 and absent entirely at web:Jer.41.9; and the same single-witness segment layer is invoked as corroboration at oshb:Jer.41.10 while the mark of identical type at oshb:Jer.41.6 is given only texture status, with the date-object distinction drawn at oshb:Jer.41.1 not drawn at oshb:Jer.41.4.
rulings.grounds: The quotation items converge on one defect class and are upheld as framed. The splices at oshb:Jer.41.6, oshb:Jer.41.8 and oshb:Jer.41.9 are each the entire verse at byte tier. The rendering paired with oshb:Jer.41.8 stops at the plea and omits “So he stopped, and didn’t kill them among their brothers.” (web:Jer.41.8), whose Hebrew is spliced in full as וַיֶּחְדַּ֕ל וְלֹ֥א הֱמִיתָ֖ם בְּת֥וֹךְ אֲחֵיהֶֽם (oshb:Jer.41.8, byte tier); the rendering paired with oshb:Jer.41.6 gives only the spoken line and omits “Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went, and as he met them, he said to them,” (web:Jer.41.6); and oshb:Jer.41.9 carries no paired rendering at all. The same unit renders oshb:Jer.41.4, oshb:Jer.41.5, oshb:Jer.41.7 and oshb:Jer.41.10 at full verse extent, so the practice is inconsistent inside one unit. Of the three affected verses only 1 is a staged continuation-paragraph fold site, so this is a gloss-extent failure in its own right and not only fold mishandling. The segment-layer item is upheld in narrowed form. Both marks are present and correctly typed as setumah at oshb:Jer.41.6 and oshb:Jer.41.10 and both are disclosed, so the disclosure sweep is complete; what is asymmetric is the argumentative use, the mark at the adopted end boundary invoked as corroboration for the reading adopted while the mark of identical type inside the span is set aside as texture without its equal implication for an internal seam being stated. Under a weak single-witness tier that corroborative force cannot be switched on at one site and off at the other. The date item is upheld and sharpened. The onset bytes read לְהָמִ֣ית אֶת גְּדַלְיָ֑הוּ (oshb:Jer.41.4, byte tier), a relative-day back-reference naming the preceding unit's own event; the site is not a member of the book's classified date-header candidate object, and the object distinction the parallel month notice receives is not drawn here. Beyond that, the back-reference itself reaches across the unit's own front seam and is nowhere disclosed as cohesion. The rest verifies: all eight splices reach byte tier, the per-site Shiloh form is claimed with no cross-site count offered, and the paseq entries at oshb:Jer.41.9 and oshb:Jer.41.10 are cited count-only. The declared heuristic false positives on this unit are confirmed.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: restore full-verse renderings beside the full-verse splices at oshb:Jer.41.6 and oshb:Jer.41.8 and supply the missing rendering for oshb:Jer.41.9. boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative: either state the equal implication of the setumah at oshb:Jer.41.6 for an internal seam there, or drop the corroboration use of the setumah at oshb:Jer.41.10; keep both disclosures either way. boundary_rationale: name the object at oshb:Jer.41.4 as the relative-day back-reference it is, state that it is not a member of the classified date-header object, and disclose it as a byte-true device reaching back across the unit's own front seam; observed_substrate_signals: re-check the date_frame key against that corrected object. Tests the cure must pass: every full-verse splice in the unit has a paired rendering of the same verse extent in the staged folded text, the checks that killed the original being the sparing clause at web:Jer.41.8, the narrated frame at web:Jer.41.6 and the absent gloss at web:Jer.41.9; the segment layer carries the same weight at both of its span-relevant sites; and no date label stands without naming the object it does and does not belong to.

rulings.challenge_claim: The closing device claim is byte-false in making the interception site the place the abduction had been heading away from, since that place is named nowhere in the abduction report; and the same sentence overstates that the closing mark closes the abductor's part in the account.
rulings.grounds: The place claim is byte-false and is upheld. The abduction report locates the seizure at אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּמִּצְפָּ֗ה (oshb:Jer.41.10, byte tier) and gives its destination as וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ לַעֲבֹ֖ר אֶל בְּנֵ֥י עַמּֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.41.10, byte tier), toward the children of Ammon. The interception place-name enters the account only at the interception itself, אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּגִבְעֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.41.12, byte tier), and again in the retrospect at מִגִּבְעֽוֹן (oshb:Jer.41.16, byte tier); the consonantal sweep returns that name in 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 3 verses), the third outside this narrative altogether. The site the abduction was heading away from is Mizpah, not the interception site, so the sentence assigns a place to a verse that does not carry it. The second, softer half of the challenge is refuted on the bytes and needs no repair. The consonantal sweep returns the abductor's name in 19 verses, none of them beyond this chapter (sweep: 19 verses); at oshb:Jer.41.16 he stands as the object of the recovery and at oshb:Jer.41.18 inside a causal back-reference to the killing already narrated. He performs no further narrated action after the escape at the unit's end verse, so reading the closing mark as closing his part in the account holds on narrative agency. The rest verifies: five full-verse splices at byte tier, renderings covering their whole verses, front-seam and closing marks both correctly typed as setumah and disclosed single-witness, and no mark, note or seg entry inside the span left undisclosed. The declared heuristic false positives are confirmed.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: replace the clause making the interception site the point the abduction was heading away from with what the bytes carry, namely that the abduction leaves Mizpah for the children of Ammon at oshb:Jer.41.10 and that the interception site first enters the account at oshb:Jer.41.12, retaining a sweep digit for the name if the name is kept. Leave the closing-mark half of the sentence as drafted. Test the cure must pass: every place the sentence assigns to a verse is present in that verse's bytes, the check that killed the original being that the interception site is absent from oshb:Jer.41.10.

rulings.challenge_claim: The exclusivity claim for the place at oshb:Jer.41.17 is dampened with a witness label where a digit-bearing sweep is owed, the identical claim-type at oshb:Jer.40.14 carrying its digit; and the closing seam warrant asserts a first joint-subject occurrence at oshb:Jer.42.1 that the bytes contradict.
rulings.grounds: Both items upheld. The exclusivity item is the same defect from both sides; the first-occurrence item is additional and only one side reached it. On the first: the device sentence claims the place is named only here in the book and offers a single-witness label where an in-sentence sweep count naming object and unit is owed, and an exclusivity claim is never tier-dampened, a witness label proving the quote and not the exclusivity. The underlying fact does hold, the bytes reading בְּגֵר֣וּת כמוהם כִּמְהָ֔ם (oshb:Jer.41.17, byte tier) with the consonantal sweeps returning the place noun in 1 verse and the qere name in 1 verse (sweep: 1 verse each), so this is a disclosure failure and not a false fact; the identical claim-type at oshb:Jer.40.14 does carry its digit, which is why the declared false-positive disposition standing on this hit in the flag queue does not hold. On the second: the closing warrant says the field captains become the account's subject together for the first time at oshb:Jer.42.1. The bytes contradict it three times, once inside this unit's own opening verse - וְיֽוֹחָנָן֙ בֶּן קָרֵ֔חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה בָּ֥אוּ (oshb:Jer.40.13, byte tier), וַיִּשְׁמַע֙ יוֹחָנָ֣ן בֶּן קָרֵ֔חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֥י הַחֲיָלִ֖ים (oshb:Jer.41.11, byte tier) and וַיִּקַּח֩ יוֹחָנָ֨ן בֶּן קָרֵ֜חַ וְכָל שָׂרֵ֧י הַחֲיָלִ֣ים (oshb:Jer.41.16, byte tier), each a joint subject of a finite verb - and the phrase stands in 9 verses book-wide (sweep: 9 verses). What is genuinely new at the seam is word order alone, וַֽיִּגְּשׁוּ֙ כָּל שָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.42.1, byte tier), fronting the captains ahead of Johanan; that is a defensible seam observation and is not what the unit claims. That sentence is also a first-occurrence claim carrying no sweep digit, so the declared false-positive disposition standing on it does not hold either. The rest verifies: three full-verse splices at byte tier, the ketiv/qere pair quoted exactly as the bytes carry it, and the front-seam, interior and closing marks all disclosed and correctly typed.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: attach an in-sentence sweep count naming the swept object and unit to the exclusivity claim, on the pattern the same claim-type already uses at oshb:Jer.40.14; the witness label cannot carry it. boundary_rationale: replace the first-occurrence claim at oshb:Jer.42.1 with the word-order observation the bytes support, or keep a first-occurrence claim only with a sweep digit that survives the phrase's book-wide count. Flag queue: re-open the declared false-positive dispositions on this unit's device_notes exclusivity hit and on its boundary_rationale first-occurrence hit. Tests the cure must pass: the exclusivity sentence carries its own digit naming object and unit; and the seam sentence survives the sweep that killed the original, the phrase already standing as joint subject at oshb:Jer.40.13, oshb:Jer.41.11 and at this unit's own opening verse.

rulings.challenge_claim: The note claims both name spellings are given as the bytes carry them, yet only one of the two forms is spliced anywhere in the unit, and the two figures are separated on a translation rendering rather than on the Hebrew.
rulings.grounds: Upheld on the bytes. The two forms are not the same spelling: וִֽיזַנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן הַמַּ֣עֲכָתִ֔י (oshb:Jer.40.8, byte tier) carries the long form closing he-vav, against the short form closing he in וִֽיזַנְיָ֖ה בֶּן הוֹשַֽׁעְיָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.42.1, byte tier). Only the second is spliced anywhere in the unit; the first appears in none of its fields, though its ref is properly carried in the evidence list. The difference is invisible in the second witness, which renders the two alike, “Jezaniah the son of the Maacathite” (web:Jer.40.8) beside “Jezaniah the son of Hoshaiah” (web:Jer.42.1), so as drafted the disambiguation rests on the patronymics in translation while the byte-level long-versus-short distinction, the live name-form hazard class here, goes unstated in the very sentence that claims to have stated it. The sweep is itself a trap at this pair: a consonantal sweep for the short spelling returns 2 verses because it matches inside the long form (sweep: 2 verses), while the long spelling returns 1 (sweep: 1 verse), so only a token-bound per-spelling read supports the claim. The rest verifies: three full-verse splices at byte tier with renderings covering their whole verses, the front-seam setumah correctly typed and disclosed single-witness, and the negative mark statement accurate, the inventories carrying no mark, note or seg entry at oshb:Jer.42.1, oshb:Jer.42.2 or oshb:Jer.42.3. The declared heuristic false positives are confirmed on their own class; this defect sits inside one of those sentences and belongs to a different class.
rulings.remedy: device_notes: splice the oshb:Jer.40.8 form beside the oshb:Jer.42.1 form with the tier named and state the long-versus-short difference explicitly, or drop the claim that both spellings are given. Test the cure must pass: every claim that forms are given as the bytes carry them has each named form spliced at its own ref and re-collated at the tier claimed, the check that killed the original being that the oshb:Jer.40.8 form appears in no field of the unit.

rulings.challenge_claim: The unit's internal-cohesion argument rests on a syntactic form claim that neither witness supports, the reply being called one unbroken sentence.
rulings.grounds: The form claim is defective and that half is upheld; the framing that the cohesion argument rests on it is not, and is corrected here. The splice opens with the narrative frame וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם יִרְמְיָ֤הוּ הַנָּבִיא֙ (oshb:Jer.42.4, byte tier), which stands outside the reply it introduces, and the verse divides internally at כְּדִבְרֵיכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.42.4, byte tier), which carries the etnachta; the second witness sets three sentence stops inside the reported speech, two of them internal (web:Jer.42.4). No morphology or syntax layer is staged, so a sentence-level form label is a byte-checkable claim held to the discipline of a digit, and here both witnesses cut against it. The operative ground is separable and byte-true, so the boundary does not depend on the label: the speaker changes on both sides, the petition closing at oshb:Jer.42.3 and a fresh reported-speech frame opening at oshb:Jer.42.5, and no internal speaker turn falls inside the verse. The negative disclosure is accurate, no mark, note or seg entry standing at oshb:Jer.42.3, oshb:Jer.42.4 or oshb:Jer.42.5, the next falling at oshb:Jer.42.6, and the single-verse span is written in the full form. The declared false-positive disposition on the flagged word holds on its own class, since the word is not an exclusivity claim owing a sweep; this defect is a different class and is not covered by that disposition.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: drop the phrase calling the reply one unbroken sentence, or restate it as the operative claim the bytes carry, a single reply with no internal speaker turn bounded by a speaker change on both sides. Test the cure must pass: no sentence-level form label survives that the verse's own internal division or either witness's own sentence punctuation contradicts, the checks that killed the original being the etnachta inside the verse and the three sentence stops in the second witness's rendering.

rulings.challenge_claim: The frame reasoning at the book's one non-initial word-event site is byte-correct, but the rendering paired with the closing verse's full-verse splice covers well under half of it, dropping the conditional frame and the obey-the-voice clause; the challenge grades this low.
rulings.grounds: The defect is real and upheld; the severity as filed is understated and is corrected here. The splice at oshb:Jer.42.13 is the entire verse at byte tier, but the rendering paired with it gives only the quoted refusal: the staged folded text opens “But if you say,” (web:Jer.42.13) and closes “so that you don’t obey Yahweh your God’s voice,” (web:Jer.42.13), and both fall out. The dropped closing clause is לְבִלְתִּ֣י שְׁמֹ֔עַ בְּק֖וֹל יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.42.13, byte tier), the obey-the-voice construction, and the dropped opening is וְאִם אֹמְרִ֣ים אַתֶּ֔ם (oshb:Jer.42.13, byte tier), the conditional frame the unit's own device note argues from when it ties this hypothetical to the conditional structure opened earlier in the span. A gloss that drops the frame the device note reasons from is not a cosmetic extent miss, and the same defect class is graded medium where it stands at web:Jer.40.14 and at web:Jer.41.8, so a low grade here is inconsistent with its own class. A second, smaller instance in the same field was named by neither challenge: the rendering paired with oshb:Jer.42.14 drops that verse's own leading frame, “saying,” (web:Jer.42.14). Neither closing verse is a staged continuation-paragraph fold site, so the truncation pattern here reaches past the fold verses. The load-bearing frame reasoning is independently verified and stands: the onset verse carries the word-event formula only after its own ten-day wait clause rather than verse-initially, and the digits match the object exactly, 21 verses carrying that formula, 20 of them verse-initial, this the single exception (sweep: 21 verses). The messenger formula at oshb:Jer.42.9 is named on its actual form without the armies element and is the scene's first, a scan of oshb:Jer.42.1 through oshb:Jer.42.8 returning none. The front-seam setumah at oshb:Jer.42.6 is correctly typed and disclosed single-witness, and no mark, note or seg entry falls inside the span. The declared heuristic false positives are confirmed.
rulings.remedy: boundary_rationale: extend the rendering paired with the oshb:Jer.42.13 splice to the whole staged folded verse, conditional frame and obey-the-voice clause included, and restore the leading frame in the rendering paired with oshb:Jer.42.14. Test the cure must pass: gloss extent equals splice extent at every ref in the unit, measured against the staged folded text, the check that killed the original being a full-verse splice at oshb:Jer.42.13 set beside a rendering covering only the quoted refusal.

supported_sample.claim_checked: The unit's onset driver: that the opening of oshb:Jer.41.1 is a month notice held apart from the book's classified reign-year date-header object rather than folded into it.
supported_sample.notes: The onset bytes read בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י (oshb:Jer.41.1, byte tier), an ordinal month notice carrying no year word and none of the bet-plus-cardinal year shape, and the site is not among the classified date-header candidates, so holding it apart from that inventory is correct and no membership is over-claimed. Checked alongside it: all three splices are full-verse at byte tier with renderings covering their whole verses in the staged folded text; both paseq entries in the span, at oshb:Jer.41.1 and oshb:Jer.41.2, are cited count-only; the front-seam mark at oshb:Jer.40.16 is correctly typed as setumah and disclosed single-witness; and no mark, note or seg entry falls at oshb:Jer.41.3, so the span-relevant disclosure is complete. One non-driving register defect worth carrying forward: the closing device sentence locates the pedigree's non-repetition by pointing at neighbouring units positionally where the convention requires a verse anchor.
